subject: bloodworm
title: Fishing Shops Sell This Worm as Bait. It Has Copper Fangs and Venom

scenes.text: Bait shops sell this worm by the dozen. It has four metal fangs.
The bloodworm hides in mud, then fires its mouth inside out like a torpedo.
At the tip sit four hollow jaws, reinforced with copper, up to about ten percent of their weight.
No other animal is known to pack that much copper into its jaws.
The fangs punch through shells and inject a venom with dozens of toxins. Even a human bite hurts.
So next time you see a bait bucket, remember: some of those worms bite back.

description:
The common bloodworm, Glycera dibranchiata, grows up to about 35 cm and attacks by everting its proboscis, which carries four hollow jaws reinforced with copper (reported as 5 to 10% of jaw weight).
The jaws can pierce shells and deliver a venom; the worm is widely sold as fishing bait.
Would you still handle bait worms after this?
first_comment: The venom is stored in a harmless form and only turns toxic on its way through the jaws. Have you ever been bitten by fishing bait?
